text:
incident-bot: ALERT 03:12 UTC — Spike in model errors for model:redwood/gpt-large-2026 on prod-us-east-1 (error rate +12% over 5m). Paging oncall. Possible bad rollout detected. :rotating_light:

sophia: @oncall-eng I'm on it. starting quick triage — checking canary logs + recent weightset changes.

devon: I saw a few 500s and also garbled token outputs reported by a couple of customers (strings with repeated "<unk>"). could be tokenizer mismatch or wrong tokenizer vocab baked into the image.

carlos: Customer-impacting? any 99th latency or request drops?

sophia: Early signs: request success rate down ~6% for requests hitting rollout fraction 0.2. Full error count in the dashboard: https://console/redwood/telemetry/rollout/rgp-large-2026

incident-bot: page sent to devon (oncall). Assigned incident severity: SEV2 due to degraded responses and B2B customer reports.

devon: I have the canary logs pulled. Looks like tokenizer.version==v2.1 was expected but deployed containers have tokenizer.version==v2.0. Also weightset manifest references quantized-bf16-v1 but the object store shows quantized-int8-v1.

irene: that sounds like two mismatched artifacts — weights and tokenizer both wrong. Could be a CI tag/manifest drift when we promoted the image.

sophia: I'm rolling up the deploy history now. deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T03:05:12 by infra-ci promoted tag release-2026-03-15-9. The tag points to image digest sha256:abcd... which maps to tokenizer:v2.0 in the image.

devon: OK that's our root cause. Release tag pointed at a previous build due to a manifest race during the publish step. Need to stop rollout and rollback to previous stable weightset + tokenizer.

sophia: Agreed. Can we toggle the rollout feature flag to kill the release? product-ops, can you flip the gate?

product-ops: Doing it now. Command: 
```
POST https://console.redwood/flags/rollouts/rgp-large-2026 -d '{"fraction":0.0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

product-ops: Flag updated. Rollout fraction set to 0.0. Canary traffic should be routed back to stable variant. :white_check_mark:

devon: Confirming — traffic rerouting in progress. Observability: canary hit counts dropping, stable variant requests rising. Latency returning to baseline.

carlos: Customer reports still showing some bad outputs — are those replayed requests pinned to older nodes?

sophia: There may be sessions using sticky routing to nodes that still have bad image cached. Asking infra to evict pods. deploy-bot: initiating rolling kill on canary pool rgp-large-2026-canary.

deploy-bot: kill/replace started: 12 pods to rotate. Command issued to k8s: 
```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/rgp-large-2026 -n inference-prod
```

irene: Meanwhile, we need to verify stable artifact checksums and ensure the correct tokenizer/weight pairing is pinned. I'm fetching manifests from artifactory.

sophia: Soph priority: verify stable weights are not corrupted. Run checksum verification: 
```
sha256sum weights/rgp-large-2026/stable/weights.tar.gz
# expect: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...
```

devon: I matched expected checksums — stable weightset OK. Problem was the released tag pointing to older build.

carlos: Any PII or customer-secret exposure risk?

sophia: No, this is functional mismatch only. No data leak. Main customer impact: malformed outputs and higher error rates for small subset of requests (~0.5% of overall traffic). We should notify affected customers.

product-ops: Preparing a short customer outreach note. Suggest: "We observed degraded text outputs for a subset of requests between 03:05-03:15 UTC due to an internal deployment mismatch. We've reverted traffic and evicted affected nodes. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

devon: Rolling back any persisted rollout state: recreating deployment with pinned image digest for stable: image@sha256:e3aa... and tokenizer v2.1 package.

sophia: I'm running a canary smoke test against the stable variant: sample prompts, check tokens and end-to-end outputs. Results: smoke passes on 8/8 samples.

deploy-bot: Pod rotation completed. All canary pods restarted with stable image digest.

irene: We're also going to add a manifest-promote preflight check to CI to prevent tag race: ensure artifact digest and tokenizer/vocab hash match before pushing release tag. Filing a ticket.

carlos: Oncall handoff — devon, do you want to remain primary or hand to carlos for next shift?

devon: I'm going offline in 20. Carlos, can you take the handoff and keep watch for any residual errors? I'll leave detailed notes in the incident doc.

carlos: taking handoff. I'll monitor error rate and customer slack threads for the next 2 hours.

sophia: Summary for postmortem: root cause = release tag race promoting incorrect image digest (tokenizer v2.0 + int8 weights) -> malformed outputs + elevated 5xx; mitigation = feature-flag kill to 0.0, pod eviction and rollback to pinned digest, checksum verification; customer impact = subset of requests with garbled tokens, ~5-10 customers reported, no data exposure; followups = CI preflight + artifact signing, add an automated manifest vs tag consistency check and add a canary-only checksum check.

product-ops: Sending customer note now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to SEV3 at 03:25 UTC. All critical mitigations complete.

devon: Leaving detailed remediation steps here for Carlos:
1) Confirm rollout fraction stays 0.0 in console.
2) Verify canary pod images: `kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.containers[0].image`
3) Run smoke test script: `scripts/smoke_canary.sh rgp-large-2026`
4) If any anomalies, escalate back to infra team and re-open pager.

carlos: Got it. A few quick notes: I'll watch the 5xx counts and sample the customer-reported requests. If nothing else in 2 hours, I'll close the thread and mark for postmortem.

irene: Filed follow-up ticket: RDW-4521 "CI manifest race causes incorrect artifact promotion". Assigned to infra-release team.

sophia: Thanks all. Good coordination. :heart:

product-ops: Closing loop with customers: sent messages to the 9 affected accounts, offering 72h support & incident summary.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — final status: rollback to stable artifact, feature flag kill applied, pods rotated, affected customers notified. See incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2768000123 for timeline.

carlos: marking handoff complete. I'll file the postmortem draft and invite infra + release leads.

sophia: I'll attach logs and checksums to the postmortem.

devon: Back tomorrow for the RCA. Night all.

carlos: Night.
